subject: Discovery synthesis & POC triage — next steps and ownership
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Bose <samir@quantify.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery synthesis & POC triage — next steps and ownership

Samir / Priya — thanks again for taking time today. Short synthesis and proposed next steps below so we have aligned scope and owners before the kickoff. Please correct me where I’m off.

TL;DR
- Problem: Quantify Labs needs accurate, low-latency entity extraction and customer-facing summarization from multi-source clinical notes to improve triage throughput and reduce manual review.
- Success metrics: 85% extraction F1 on the priority entity set, average 300ms 95th‑pct latency for <512 token requests, and a 25% reduction in manual review time for triage team.
- Proposed initial POC: 4-week pilot (2-week ingestion + tuning, 2-week eval/runbook). Red-teamed prompt set + eval harness.

Key pain points we heard
- High variability in note templates across clinics causes extraction drift.
- Current pipeline takes 8–12s per document for downstream enrichment (not acceptable).
- Compliance: data residency and short retention window; needs SOC2-level evidence and a minimal access footprint.

Proposed POC scope (what we’ll deliver)
1) Ingestion connectors: s3 drop + limited SFTP sample load for up to 10k anonymized records.
2) Model serving: Redwood hosted POC using a quantized open model (custom routing to a lower-latency variant when needed).
3) Prompt/eval: 250 prompt variants covering edge templates + a 500-sample labeled eval set.
4) Metrics and dashboard: token-level latency, per-prompt precision/recall, and a weekly regression alert.
5) Hand-over: action playbook and integration checklist for your infra team.

Owners (initial)
- Redwood PM: Marcus Lin (on this thread) — scope/strategy and customer outcomes.
- Redwood Ops: Kimberly Park — access, infra, and observability setup.
- Redwood Applied ML: Soojin Lee — prompt design, evals, and quality gates.
- Quantify Labs: Samir Bose — data steward and product owner; Priya Mehta — security/compliance lead.

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): sign-off on POC charter, HubSpot deal + NDA acknowledgment.
- Week 1: data access + initial s3 transfer (5k sample).
- Week 2: baseline runs, prompt tuning, first eval snapshot.
- Week 3: stress/lossless latency tuning, dashboarding.
- Week 4: final eval, handover meeting, runbook delivery.

Immediate asks from Quantify Labs
- Provide a 5k anonymized sample (s3 link or SFTP credentials) by Mon 10/12.
- Confirm retention window and whether payloads must be redacted prior to transfer.
- Security questionnaire: completed SOC2 attestation and any specific DLP constraints.

Attachments
- I’ve attached an initial POC charter (redwood-poc-charter-v1.pdf) and a sample prompt/eval matrix (prompt-evals-sample.csv).

Next meeting
- Propose Wed 10/14 11:00am PT for kickoff and to review the first transfer. If that works for you I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samir Bose <samir@quantify.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya@acclaris.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 17:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery synthesis & POC triage — next steps and ownership

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal readout. Quick clarifications and a couple asks: 

Clarifications
- The 5k sample: will include variations from our 3 highest-volume clinics; we will pseudonymize PHI but leave structure intact (we will not redact clinical codes unless you require).
- Retention: we need a 30‑day max retention window for POC artifacts; is that configurable on Redwood hosted POCs?

Asks
1) Can you add a small eval for entity-level confidence calibration? Our downstream rule engine uses confidence thresholds and we need that signal exposed.
2) Security: Priya will send the specific DLP constraints (regexes to scrub); do you have a preferred format for mapping rules (CSV / JSON)?

Kickoff time OK on 10/14 11:00am PT — accept tentative until we confirm S3 link. We’ll aim to drop the sample by 10/12 EOB.

Samir
Head of Product, Quantify Labs
samir@quantify.ai | +1 (212) 555-4422

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery synthesis & POC triage — next steps and ownership

Adding a couple ops notes from my side.

1) Retention: yes, Redwood hosted POC can enforce a 30-day retention policy and we’ll provide export+purge logs at handover. I’ll add the retention SLA to the charter and share an updated PDF by Friday.

2) Data transfer options: S3 (preferred) or limited SFTP. For S3 please provide an object manifest (CSV) with: original_filename, clinic_id, pseudo_id, ingestion_date. That helps our mapping.

3) VPC/Networking: If Quantify wants to test a private path we can stand up a limited VPC peering for the POC (no cross-account keys). That will add ~3 business days to infra prep — call it Week 1+buffer.

4) Confidence signals: Soojin — can you include a column for entity_confidence in the eval output? That will help the calibration ask.

I’ll attach a minimal manifest template and the updated charter once I finish edits.

—
Kimberly Park
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
